name: Descriptive Statistics
description: Types of data and graphs, primary and secondary data collection, questionnaire design, central tendency, dispersion, moments, skewness, kurtosis, correlation and simple linear regression.

name: Introduction to Data Science
description: Data science process, SQL for data science, document and graph databases, data pre-processing, feature generation and selection, decision trees, random forests, association rules, text mining and SVMs.

name: Calculus (with Calculus Lab)
description: Limits, continuity, differentiation, partial derivatives, Jacobians, mean value theorems, Taylor and Maclaurin series, maxima and minima, curve tracing and multiple integrals; lab work visualises these computationally.
audience: Learners preparing for data science mathematics
review_note: Theory and lab share the same course code (17200105). The lab's reference links point to MATLAB differential-equation tutorials rather than calculus material; the lab software is not otherwise named.

name: Analytics using Excel
description: Spreadsheet functions, data import and cleaning, cell referencing, lookups, logical and statistical functions, PivotTables, PivotCharts, consolidation and worksheet formatting.

name: Probability & Distribution Theory
description: Probability definitions, conditional probability, Bayes' theorem, random variables, joint and marginal distributions, expectation, moment generating functions, binomial, Poisson and normal distributions and the central limit theorem.
review_note: Page 15 of the PDF is blank.

name: Linear Algebra
description: Matrices, rank, systems of linear equations, Gauss and Gauss-Jordan elimination, vector spaces, linear transformations, inner product spaces, Gram-Schmidt, eigenvalues and diagonalisation.
audience: Learners preparing for machine learning and data science
review_note: Course Outcome 5 ('continuous and discrete probability and distribution') duplicates an outcome from the probability course and does not match the linear algebra content.

name: Differential Equations (with Differential Equations Lab)
description: First-order and exact equations, integrating factors, orthogonal trajectories, linear equations with constant and variable coefficients, variation of parameters and simultaneous equations; the lab solves ODEs and systems in MATLAB.
review_note: Lab practicals 3 and 4 are near duplicates ('first order linear ODE').

name: Introduction to R Programming
description: R objects, reading and writing data, sequences, data manipulation, matrix computation, graphics, descriptive statistics, frequency distributions and probability distributions in R.
audience: Analysts and researchers new to R

name: Time Series Analysis (with Time Series Analysis Lab)
description: Time-series components, additive and multiplicative models, trend measurement, seasonal indices, AR and MA processes, ACF, Yule-Walker estimation, exponential smoothing and index numbers.
review_note: Lab header lists L-T-P as 2-0-4 but the contact hours give 0 lectures and 60 practicals; lab objectives mention visualising proportions, which the practical list does not cover.

name: Inferential Statistics
description: Sampling distributions, properties of estimators, maximum likelihood, hypothesis testing framework, Neyman-Pearson lemma, large-sample tests, chi-square, t and F tests, and one- and two-way ANOVA.

name: Operations Research
description: Linear programming formulation and graphical solution, convex sets, simplex, Big-M and two-phase methods, duality, transportation and assignment problems, and two-person zero-sum games.
review_note: Course Outcome 4 mentions sequencing problems, which do not appear in the unit content.

name: Programming with Python
description: Installing and running Python, debugging, values and types, variables, expressions, conditionals, loops and control statements, reading files and plotting data.
review_note: Course Outcomes 4 and 5 are identical ('plot data using appropriate Python visualization libraries'); units do not cover lists, functions or plotting although objectives mention them.

name: Machine Learning-I (with ML-I Lab)
description: Learning approaches, numerical representation, norms and matrix decompositions, optimisation and gradient descent, linear regression, bias-variance trade-off, MLE, trees, bagging, random forests, SVM, naive Bayes, k-means, kNN and gradient boosting.
audience: Analysts and developers entering machine learning
review_note: Lab practical list skips items 4-5 and then repeats numbers 6-8; item 7 text is garbled (accuracy/precision phrase inserted mid-sentence).

name: Mathematical Foundations of Data Science
description: Probability review, concentration inequalities, PAC learning, importance and priority sampling, simple and multiple regression, cross-validation, ridge and lasso, gradient descent, SVD, eigenvectors and the power method.
review_note: Frequency is marked Odd although the module sits in Semester IV (even); other Semester IV modules are marked Even.

name: Statistical Quality Control and Demography
description: Quality concepts and TQM, chance and assignable causes, statistical basis of control charts, ARL, X-bar/R and X-bar/s charts, p and np charts, single and double sampling plans with OC and ASN functions.
review_note: Title includes 'Demography' but the module contains no demography content; only the SQC material is used.

name: Research Methodology
description: Types of research, research process, problem definition, literature review, research design, mathematical and empirical models, model evaluation and simulation studies.
review_note: Objectives refer to 'M.Sc. students' although this is a B.Sc. syllabus; the description mentions ethics and qualitative/mixed methods but units do not cover them in detail.

name: Machine Learning-II (with ML-II Lab)
description: Multilayer perceptrons, back-propagation, CNNs, transfer learning, RNNs, training techniques, decision trees and ensembles (stacking, bagging, boosting), and NLP with LSTM and attention.
review_note: Lab includes a genetic algorithm practical not covered in the theory units.

name: Matrix Computations for Data Science (with Lab)
description: Gaussian elimination, LU and Cholesky, QR factorisation, least-squares problems, SVD and numerical rank, sensitivity, and eigenvalue algorithms; lab uses Excel, MATLAB and Mathematica.
review_note: Lab description and outcomes describe introductory linear algebra and general tasks (binary numbers, PDEs, integrals) rather than the theory's matrix-computation content; theory objectives mention discretisation 'of singular value decomposition', which appears garbled.

name: Discrete Mathematics
description: Sets, relations, counting, recurrence relations, propositional logic, lattices, Boolean algebra, Karnaugh maps, switching circuits and graph theory including shortest paths and spanning trees.
audience: Learners with a computer science interest
review_note: Candidate for knowledge-hub articles or an optional mathematics module. Its graph theory unit overlaps with the separate Graph Theory module (p80-81).

name: Sampling Techniques
description: Sample survey steps, sampling frames, SRSWOR and SRSWR, proportions, stratified, cluster and systematic sampling, and regression estimators.
review_note: Course description appears to be copied from another institution ('our introductory statistics course', 'offered every two to three years'); objectives mention two-phase and multistage designs and survey weights that are not in the units.

name: Design of Experiment
description: Principles of experimentation, ANOVA, CRD, RBD and LSD with missing observations, two- and three-level factorial and fractional factorial designs, split-plot and strip arrangements.

name: Pattern Recognition
description: Pattern recognition system design, Bayesian decision theory, histogram, kernel and kNN methods, Parzen-window networks, instar/outstar and competitive networks, self-organising maps, SVM and multilayer networks.
review_note: Course Outcome 5 refers to parametric and non-parametric statistical test models, which differs from the density-estimation sense of 'parametric/non-parametric methods' in Unit 2.

name: Introduction to LaTeX
description: Installing LaTeX, document classes, page layout, formatting, mathematics, tables, images, BibTeX bibliographies and Beamer presentations.
review_note: Objective 3 ('classifies non-linear programming problems') is unrelated to LaTeX and appears to be a copy error.

name: Applied Multivariate Statistical Analysis (with Lab)
description: Multivariate data exploration, multivariate normal distribution, tests of linear hypotheses, partial and multiple correlation, discriminant analysis, logistic regression, PCA, biplots, factor analysis and cluster analysis; lab adds runs and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests.
review_note: Lab description mentions canonical correlation and MANOVA/MANCOVA, which are not in the theory units or the practical list.

name: Reliability & Survival Analysis (with Lab)
description: Survival and hazard functions, IFR/DFR classes, lifetime distributions, censoring schemes, Kaplan-Meier and Nelson-Aalen estimators, Q-Q and hazard plots, and reliability of series, parallel, k-out-of-n and standby systems.
review_note: Cox proportional hazards and log-rank tests are named in the course description but not in the units. Objectives describe multiple linear regression, which does not match the content. Description lists SAS, JMP, STATA, R or S+ while the lab is built on SPSS.

name: Business Analytics
description: Business intelligence architecture, role of mathematical models, data mining and warehousing overview, data validation and transformation, and the analytics process including descriptive, predictive, social media and behavioural analytics.
review_note: Unit 4 lists 'Perspective' analytics, presumably a typo for 'Prescriptive'. Objectives mention clustering algorithms that are not in the units.

name: Data Visualization and Modelling
description: Mapping data to aesthetics, coordinate systems, colour scales, visualising amounts, distributions, proportions, trends and geospatial data, including Q-Q plots, choropleths and cartograms.
review_note: Course description refers to a third-party (TCS iON) online certification programme lasting five to six months; this must not be reproduced or implied. Header lists 60 lectures but units total 30.

name: Graph Theory
description: Graphs and subgraphs, walks and paths, trees and spanning trees, binary tree traversal, prefix codes, chromatic numbers and polynomials, dominating sets and directed graphs.
review_note: Candidate for knowledge-hub articles or an optional mathematics module. Overlaps with Unit 4 of Discrete Mathematics; objectives mention planar graphs, which the units do not cover.

name: Operating System
description: Computer system overview, processes and threads, CPU scheduling, memory management, virtual memory and file systems.
review_note: Not relevant to a statistics, mathematics and data-science consultancy offering.

name: Hadoop Programming
description: Hadoop features, HDFS, cluster anatomy and daemons, HDFS shell commands, cluster setup, and MapReduce applications including matrix multiplication, combiners and joins.
review_note: Course outcomes mention NoSQL with MongoDB and Cassandra, but the practical list contains no NoSQL exercises.

name: Database Management System (with DBMS Lab)
description: DBMS components, data models, ER diagrams and UML, normalisation, SQL queries, subqueries, joins, constraints and views; lab covers table design, triggers, stored procedures and cursors in MySQL.
review_note: Theory module is marked DSE while its lab is marked Core.

name: Big Data Analytics (with Lab)
description: Big data characteristics and applications, Hadoop ecosystem, schedulers, cluster setup, MapReduce, Pig, Hive, Spark, Spark SQL, PySpark pipelines, k-means and frequent itemset mining.
applications: Marketing, retail, hospitality, consumer goods and defence analytics
review_note: Lab section headings are numbered 14-26 instead of 1-13 (template error).

name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
description: AI history, uninformed and informed search, hill climbing, simulated annealing, A* and AO*, constraint satisfaction, knowledge representation, rule-based systems, reasoning under uncertainty and syntactic analysis.
review_note: Only partially relevant: search algorithms and knowledge representation are outside the core statistics offering; 'reasoning under uncertainty' could support an article. Course Outcome 5 mentions data mining projects, unrelated to the content.

name: Fuzzy Logic & Fuzzy Decision Making
description: Fuzzy sets, alpha-cuts, extension principle, t-norms, fuzzy relations, fuzzy logic and inference, multicriteria decision making, fuzzy ranking, fuzzy linear programming and defuzzification.
review_note: Used only for its decision-making unit (p99); description mentions nonlinear integrals and possibility theory, which are not in the units.

name: Introduction of Stochastic Process
description: Classification of stochastic processes, Markov chains and transition matrices, stationary distributions, Poisson and birth-death processes, and Markovian and non-Markovian queuing models.
review_note: Course description mentions reliability applications but units contain no reliability content beyond queuing.

name: Numerical Method
description: Errors, root finding (bisection, secant, Regula Falsi, Newton-Raphson, Graeffe), interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration, direct and iterative linear solvers, and eigenvalue methods.
review_note: Course code 17200710 follows 17200708; no 17200709 appears in the PDF. Numerical solution of IVPs is in the unit title but no specific ODE methods are listed.

name: Deep Learning Techniques
description: Overfitting and regularisation, feedforward networks, back-propagation, optimisation for deep models, batch normalisation, convolutional networks, RNNs, LSTM, GANs and deep learning applications.
review_note: Deep-learning consulting requires the owner to confirm in-house capacity before launch.

name: Introduction to Decision Modelling
description: Payoff matrices, decision making under risk, value of information, Bayes' theorem and decision trees, non-cooperative game theory and Nash equilibria, and discrete-event and Monte-Carlo simulation.

name: Introduction to Financial Mathematics
description: Progressions, growth and decay, interest and time value of money, discrete compounding and payment series, production functions including Cobb-Douglas, and market theory and profit maximisation.
review_note: Description promises portfolio selection, CAPM, Black-Scholes and actuarial exam (SOA FM/MFE) topics that are absent from the units; course outcomes describe microeconomics. Only unit content should be used, and no actuarial-exam claims should be made.

name: Data Mining and Data Warehousing
description: Data pre-processing and cleaning, concept description, attribute relevance, cluster analysis (partitioning, hierarchical, density-based) and data warehousing with data cubes, star and snowflake schemas.
review_note: Description mentions association analysis and numeric prediction, which are not in the units.

name: Mathematical Economics
description: Constrained and unconstrained optimisation in economics, linear and non-linear programming with production and diet problems, Hawkins-Simon conditions, input-output analysis, game theory and difference equations.
review_note: PDF spells 'Hawkin-Simon conditions' (standard: Hawkins-Simon).
